newsitem.title: USA: Massachusetts Mutual outlines merger cost savings.
newsitem.headline: Massachusetts Mutual outlines merger cost savings.

text.p: Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance Co, which merged in March with Connecticut Mutual Life Insurance Co, said Thursday the merger reduced expenses in 1996 for the combined company by $108 million, about $26 million "ahead of plan."
"By every significant measure, the merger has already yielded important benefits for the combined company and its policyholders," Chairman and Chief Executive Thomas Wheeler said in a statement.
Wheeler said that additional cost savings have been identified that should bring the total annual savings to $148 million in 1997.

"These annualized expense savings, initially expected to be achieved over three years, rather than one year, contribute to the company's ongoing financial strength, dividend capacity and ability to grow," Wheeler added.
The company also said it paid $860 million in dividends in 1996, a five percent increase from dividends paid in the prior year.
